newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on exports.

text.p: Surprisingly high USDA weekly export sales data and short covering ahead of Monday's USDA quarterly stocks report pushed soybeans to a sharply higher close on Thursday, traders said.

"Beans were up with meal on the export sales," said Jack Scoville, analyst with LIT America. "Demand has been good enough that the U.S. markets have been very competitive with the South American markets, which is incredibly unusual for this time of year."
USDA put weekly soybean export sales at 387,000 tonnes, and soymeal sales at a higher-than-expected 209,800 tonnes.
Soybeans ended 14 to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher with May up 14 at $8.55 a bushel.

Scoville and others said they had anticipated the U.S. export pace would slow as Brazil began exporting. But equipment problems and strikes at two Brazilian ports put exports off to a slow pace and buyers continued to rely on U.S. supplies as evidenced by USDA's export data, they said.

"It looks like we've got one more round (of U.S. purchases) before they'll switch to Brazilian," a floor source said. "They're just not ready to take a chance on broken conveyor belts slowing loadings."

Trade was said to be sporatic on the day with frenzied shortcovering noted in the final 15 minutes of trade. Floor sources said traders were unwilling to go into a three-day weekend with short positions, especially ahead of Monday's USDA quarterly stocks and planting intentions report.

Analysts expected Monday's report to show plantings at 65.85 million acres, above last year's 64.21 million. Stocks were expected to total 1.093 billion bushels, compared with last year's levels of 1.190 billion.
Funds bought at least 15 million bushels on the day. Refco Inc, USA Trading and Prudential Securities each bought three million bushels May. CIS and ADM each bought 2.5 million May.
Sellers were few and far between but some floor sources reported small-lot South American hedging above $8.60 per bushel in the May and July.
In options, Refco sold 400 May $8.75 calls at 20-1/2 cents. Merrill Lynch bought 400 May $8.50 calls at 29 to 31 cents.
Soybean volume was estimated at 56,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 37,713 contracts.
